findings.title: Task 2's "suite passes unchanged" gate is unachievable as written
findings.description: Task 2 replaces `PythonAdapter.metrics = frozenset(SnapshotMetric)` (confirmed at `src/squadron/metrology/snapshot/python_adapter.py:105`) with an explicit four-metric set, while adding four members to the enum. `tests/metrology/snapshot/test_python_length.py:60` asserts `adapter.metrics == set(SnapshotMetric)`, so once `SnapshotMetric` has eight members that assertion is false by construction. Task 2's Success line — "the full `tests/metrology/` suite passes unchanged" — therefore contradicts itself, and Task 2 says nothing about touching that test. A junior implementer hits a red gate with no sanctioned route and is likely to either revert the metrics change (which is the one thing that prevents `take_snapshot` from raising, per the DEVLOG "Surprise" note) or hand-edit a test outside any listed task. Fix: state the assertion edit inside Task 2 ("update `test_adapter_declares_its_metrics_and_pb2_conventions` to the explicit set"), or restate the gate as "the suite passes after that one assertion update." The same file also shows `TypeScriptAdapter` already declaring an explicit set, so only the Python assertion is affected (`test_typescript_length.py:42` uses a `not in` check and survives).

findings.title: Success Criterion 10's "other metrics are unchanged" clause has no test
findings.description: The slice design's criterion 10 reads "`duplicated_lines` as `tool_failed` with a WARNING naming the count and the ceiling, **and its other metrics are unchanged**", and the failure-mode table's row 2 carries the same claim ("Other metrics are unaffected"). Task 10 implements it and Task 11 asserts `tool_failed` plus the WARNING over the pure `measure_duplication` function with a whitespace test tokenizer, so there are no other metrics in scope to compare. Tasks 13/15 exercise duplication through the adapters but never trip the ceiling, and Task 26's snapshot-level tests don't either. The slice's own Technical Requirement ("Failure-mode tests assert both the signal and the outcome for each row of the failure-mode table") is therefore only half-satisfied for that row. Cheap close: one adapter-level case (Task 13 or Task 15) with `DUPLICATION_MAX_TOKENS` monkeypatched down, asserting file length, function length, complexity and lint are byte-identical to the same run without the ceiling.

findings.title: No load test for the duplication pass's restated memory/throughput bound
findings.description: The slice restates a resource NFR in D3: "~133 bytes per token, measured on 20261023 at squadron's size: 0.95M Python tokens gave 120 MiB… a repo ten times squadron's size needs over 1 GiB… `DUPLICATION_MAX_TOKENS = 4_000_000` (about 530 MiB)". `project-documents/ai-project-guide/project-guides/rules/python.md:57` requires a `tests/load/` test asserting latency, throughput or resource bounds for code on the environment-layer path, and CI gating for slices touching it. The task breakdown has no `tests/load/` task: Task 11's ceiling case lowers the constant via monkeypatch, which proves the branch exists but never validates the constant at realistic scale — which is precisely what 4M tokens and the 133 bytes/token figure claim. The walkthrough (Task 29, steps 1–10) also has no scale step. Add one load task over squadron- or context-forge-sized input asserting the token count and a memory/time bound against the D3 figures. If that task is added, it needs a paired CI wiring task so the gate is explicit rather than implied — the current breakdown leaves no such hook.

findings.title: Task 26's both-languages coverage case needs a stated report source
findings.description: "a Python+TypeScript repo with a fresh report covering files of both languages gives present coverage for each" requires one Cobertura report holding entries for both ecosystems, but the Task 18 fixtures are single-producer (coverage.py covers `src/squadron`, Istanbul covers the scratch TS project). Either say the test composes a small hand-written two-`<source>` report, or split the case into "Python present via the coverage.py fixture; TypeScript present via the Istanbul fixture". Task 24 already covers the mismatched-language half at unit level ("a reading with none of the language's files gives empty `per_file` and every file in `tool_ignored_files`"), so only the adapter-level positive case is under-specified.

findings.title: Commit markers are checklist items; placement is sound
findings.description: The markers are written as `- [ ] Commit: …` rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines. That matches AGENTS.md ("Use checklist format for all task files. Each item and subitem should have a `[ ]` checkbox") and the precedent in 400's task file, so I record it as convention reconciliation, not a defect. Substantively the placement is right: Tasks 3, 5, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 19, 21, 23, 25 (implementation) have no commit and their following test task does — one commit per tested unit, not one per task and not all deferred to the end.

findings.title: Task 1 is a single-checkbox task
findings.description: Branch creation from the target with one success line could sit as the first step of Task 2 without loss. 30 tasks against ~10 new modules, two captured real-report fixtures, an XML reader, a rolling-hash window pass, a freshness check, preflight validation, render, docs and a ten-step walkthrough is proportionate for this slice; Task 10 (Effort 4) is the heaviest single task but is coherent as one module and is fully covered by Task 11's eight cases, so I am not asking for a split.

findings.title: Criteria-to-task mapping holds apart from the two gaps above
findings.description: All twelve functional criteria, the five technical requirements and both integration requirements trace to named tasks: 1→8/12/14, 2→7/9, 3→4/6, 4→11/13/15, 5→21/22/26, 6→19/20/23, 7→18/20/23/24, 8→19/20/23/24, 9→16/17, 10→10/11 (signal half only, see CONCERN), 11→23/26/29, 12→7/8; real Cobertura fixtures→18, line-count diffs and the enum-only `snapshot_models.py` check→30, docs plus the "old snapshots are skipped and must be retaken" statement→28, walkthrough steps 1–10→29 with the missing-400-record case handled explicitly. I found no scope creep: every task cites a decision (D1–D6) or a component from the slice's module table, and the two contingency instructions (move a tokenizer to `python_tokens.py`/`typescript_tokens.py` if a module passes ~300 lines, and record grammar-node differences in D2) are amendment hooks the design itself anticipates rather than new scope. Sequencing is clean and acyclic: enums → per-language counters with their tests → `MeasuredFunction`/`measure_parse_metrics` → complexity measurement then integration tests → duplication core then each language's tokenizer → coverage key/preflight → fixtures → reader → freshness → measurements → adapter wiring → snapshot tests → render → docs → walkthrough → validation. Task 3/5's exported `counting` text feeds Task 8, Task 7's read-and-decode helper feeds Task 10, and Task 18's captured root `version`/`<source>` facts feed Task 19 — dependencies run in the listed direction throughout.
